args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 unhealthy in all regions, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to all production regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) failed health checks, with an error rate of ~18%. Remediation: rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production (v2.3.1 was the latest deploy and is unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc on staging is also unhealthy). Rollback completed and verified — all regions now report v2.3.0. Impact during the incident window: elevated error rates on checkout-api affecting checkout flows. Next steps: confirm error rates have returned to baseline, investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before re-deploying, and open a post-incident review.

trace.final:
Done. Summary of actions:

**Investigation**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), reporting **unhealthy** with an **18% error rate**.
- Release history showed v2.3.1 as the latest production deploy with `unhealthy` status, and `v2.3.1-rc` unhealthy in staging as well. The most recent **healthy in production** release was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback**
- Rolled `checkout-api` back to **v2.3.0** across all production regions. Result: `rolled_out`, `VERIFIED` — all regions now report v2.3.0.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for `checkout-api` (on-call paged), summarizing the 18% error rate on v2.3.1, the rollback to v2.3.0 in all regions, and next steps (confirm error rate returns to baseline, root-cause the v2.3.1 health check failures before re-deploying, post-incident review).

Note: no approval was required here since v2.3.0 was a version previously healthy in production — only deploying a never-healthy version would need change-manager sign-off.
